newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles voters approve $2.4 bln school bond.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles voters approve $2.4 bln school bond.

text.p: Voters in Los Angeles approved a $2.4 billion bond measure for Los Angeles Unified School District, according to semi-official election returns Wednesday.
No other school district in the country has ever approved a bond issue of this size, the measure's supporters said.

With 100 percent of the precincts reporting, the Los Angeles bond measure had won the approval of 70.98 percent of the voters, city election officials said. The measure required 66.67 percent approval for passage.
"This is a victory for all of Los Angeles," said Erik Nasarenko, a spokesman for the bond campaign. "These are basic brick and mortar repairs that every school needed."
The measure authorizes Los Angeles Unified School District to issue $2.4 billion of general obligation bonds to fund improvements at more than 800 schools.

By law, expenditures can only be made for school buildings, classrooms and school grounds. No money from the sale of the bonds can be used for administrators' salaries. Each project will be monitored by an independent oversight committee, according to the school district.

Bond proceeds will be used to replace deteriorating roofing, heating, plumbing and electrical systems. The bonds will also fund earthquake reinforcement and asbestos removal, as well as class-size reduction programs.
The bonds would be repaid over a period not to exceed 25 years by a property tax levied on property owners in the school district, according to the proposition.
Last November, an identical Los Angeles Unified School District bond measure narrowly failed.
